title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of Grothendieck's comparison of the 'lacets' (loop) groups and Teichmüller groups of types (0,4) and (1,1). This is the topological and anabelian form of the classical fact that an elliptic curve is a double cover of P^1 branched at 4 points.

Setup (previous page):
- π̃ is an outer group of type (0,4), i.e. the fundamental group of a sphere minus 4 points.
- One cusp i_0 is distinguished, so that I(π̃) = {i_0} ⊔ I(π), where π is of type (0,3) and |I(π)| = 3.
- Abelianisation gives π̃_ab ≅ T^{I(π̃)}, where T is the orientation module.
- There is a canonical outer homomorphism π̃ → Z/2. It sends each cusp generator to 1: it is (π̃_ab)_2 ≅ (Z/2)^{I(π̃)} followed by the sum of coefficients.
- Its kernel π̃' is a loop group of type (1,4). This is Riemann–Hurwitz: a double cover of the sphere branched at all 4 punctures has genus 1, and each puncture has a single preimage.

This page:
- Choosing a representative of π̃ in its outer class gives an honest exact sequence (68): 1 → π̃' → π̃ → Z/2 → 1.
- Because the cover is totally ramified, the cusps correspond bijectively: (69) I(π̃') ≅ I(π̃).
- 'Plugging the relative holes' means filling the three cusps lying over I(π) ⊂ I(π̃). This yields a group of type (1,1), carrying a Z/2-action. Grothendieck notes that this action is just the canonical one, i.e. the elliptic involution −1.

The subtle point is that π̃ → Z/2 is only an outer homomorphism. Its kernel is therefore determined only up to the extra outer action of the Z/2-symmetry. So the construction yields slightly less than an object of C^ext_{1,1}: a 'symmetrised' object. To get a genuine object one must choose a kernel π̃'. That choice is a choice of an object in a Z/2-gerbe, a banded gerbe with Z/2 as fundamental group (continued on the next page).

The point of all this, stated on the next page, is a canonical isomorphism, modulo inner automorphisms, T_{1,1}/{±1} ≅ 𝔖_{0,3}. Here T_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z) and 𝔖_{0,3} is the relevant (0,4)-with-a-marked-point / (0,3) symmetry group. Grothendieck argues this is conceptually independent of the identification T_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z), and he cautions against simply identifying 𝔖_{0,3} with GL(2,Z)/±1.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument is explicitly heuristic: the next page says 'modulo une vérification plus soignée'.
The kernel of an outer homomorphism is ill-defined. Grothendieck himself flags this and repairs it with the gerbe formulation, so it is a recognised gap rather than an error.

ideas.what: The type-(1,4) group is the kernel of the 'sum of cusp coefficients' map π_{0,4} → Z/2, i.e. the elliptic curve as the double cover of P^1 branched at 4 points.
ideas.modern_name: Hyperelliptic / Legendre double cover; elliptic involution
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the (0,4)/(1,1) relation at low complexity

ideas.what: Mapping class / Teichmüller group of (1,1) modulo ±1 is identified with the (0,4)-type symmetry group via filling the branch cusps.
ideas.modern_name: Birman–Hilden theorem (symmetric mapping class groups); Mod(S_{1,1})/⟨ι⟩ ≅ PSL(2,Z)

ideas.what: The kernel of an outer homomorphism is defined only up to a Z/2 symmetry; choosing it is choosing an object of a Z/2-banded gerbe.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of M_{1,1}: M_{1,1} as a μ_2-gerbe over its rigidification; outer extensions and nonabelian H^2 / gerbes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful conceptual re-derivation of the classical (1,1) ↔ (0,4) correspondence. The gerbe-theoretic treatment of the ±1 ambiguity in the outer (anabelian) setting is a nice touch. However, it matches known material: Birman–Hilden, and M_{1,1} as a μ_2-gerbe.
transcription_corrections: 'on aura[?] une[?] donc[?] on a une suite exacte' likely reads 'on aura en fait une suite exacte'.
'π̃' est un groupe induit[?]' should probably read 'π̃' est un groupe à lacets'.
'En bornant[?] les termes relatifs[?]' should read 'En bouchant les trous relatifs'.
'I(π_0)' is likely 'I(π)' (the 3-element set). The clause 'qui est de cardinal 3' refers to I(π).
'Mais en fonction des relations[?] - intuitions[?] des deux faits' is uncertain; it is perhaps 'Mais en fonction des choix des deux faits'.
'c'est un tel itinéraire[?], "un des[?] symétrisé"' likely reads 'c'est un tel élément, "un objet symétrisé"'.
'il faut avoir "choisi un objet" π̃'' likely reads 'il faut avoir "choisi un noyau" π̃''.
'ou dire que groupe extérieur' likely reads 'on dira que pour l'homom. extérieur ...'.
'312' at the start of the next page is the page number, not an exponent: the text reads 'dans une (Z/2Z)-gerbe'.
